title: All-hands priorities refocus — scratch notes
body:
Purpose / quick goal:
- Draft rapid, honest framing for the upcoming all-hands (30–40m). Leadership asked for a lean update that resets top priorities and gives org clarity on where to focus this quarter.
- This is a scratchpad — keep tone direct, avoid script-y language. Leave room for CEO color.

Opening 60–90s (framing options):
- Option A (blunt): "We shipped a lot, but growth of complexity is outpacing our ability to operate. Today is about refocusing on 3 things that matter to customers and to our unit economics."
- Option B (calmer): "We have momentum; now we need to channel it. I'm going to share three practical priorities that will shape what we deprioritize."
- Note to self: pick Option B if CEO wants softer tone; A if urgency required.

Three priority pillars (single-line summaries + 1 example):
1) Predictable latency & cost (SLOs + Optimize push)
   - Why: customers sign on to predictable per-request economics; internal ops/finance need fewer surprises.
   - Example deliverable: aggressive rollout of two Optimize recommendations (batching + config presets) to top 10 customers by end of month.

2) Enterprise readiness (Private + Dedicated reliability):
   - Why: large deals are getting gated by audit/KMS and private control; closing these drives ARR stability.
   - Example deliverable: ship hardened install docs + one-week on-call rotation for Private pilot.

3) Quality-safe experimentation (model rollouts / evals):
   - Why: we need to move fast without regressing quality for production customers.
   - Example deliverable: mandatory canary + eval checklist for any model change in hosted API.

What this means (operationally):
- Small cross-functional strike teams for each pillar (4–6 people) with clear weekly milestones.
- A public cadence: 2-week updates in #company and a one-pager for execs.
- Deprioritize: a list of features that can be shelved or delayed (pulling together names next).

Anticipated questions / suggested answers (Q&A crib):
Q: "Will deprioritizing reduce product velocity?"
A: "Short-term maybe on some feature bets; long-term it frees cycles for high-impact work and reduces operational debt."

Q: "How will success be measured?"
A: "Each team will own 1–2 metrics tied to a pillar (latency p95, cost per token, private pilot SLA attainment, eval pass-rate). We’ll publish a simple dashboard weekly."

Q: "Are there layoffs or budget cuts?"
A: "No blanket cuts. We’re reallocating focus and funding toward pillars; specific role changes (if any) will be handled through managers and People. Transparency is important — we’ll share updates."

Q: "How long is this focus expected to last?"
A: "We expect an intentional 8–12 week focus period; after that we’ll assess and either extend or broaden priorities."

Microscript / quick lines for CEO to use (bullet bank):
- "This is about predictability — for customers and for our team."
- "We will be ruthless about measurement and honest about trade-offs."
- "You’ll see tangible outputs in the next sprint or two, not just more meetings."

Action items before all-hands (TODAY / next 48h):
- Finalize the 3 pillars and one concrete deliverable for each — Rhea to sync with Jonas and Mikaela.
- Assemble one slide per pillar (owner + metric + milestone). Owner: Jonas.
- Draft 2-slide CEO opener (pick tone) — Mikaela to draft.
- Publish a short pre-read (one pager) in #company 24h before meeting — Rhea.

Unresolved / risky points to surface in the meeting if asked:
- We need clearer runway on Dedicated GPU capacity in eu-west region; may affect demo cadence for sales.
- There are ongoing SRE tickets tied to streaming stability that might require temporary rate-limits; be prepared to explain customer impact.

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep language concrete. People are tired of abstract 'focus' memos that don't change day-to-day.
- Use examples customers will understand (ex: "reduced 99th percentile latency for checkout flow from 1.2s to 0.6s").
- Avoid internal jargon in the all-hands — keep it approachable for non-engineering.
- Let managers know we'll ask them for team-level commitments the following week.

Follow-ups after all-hands (draft cadence):
- Week 1: pillar kickoff notes + team assignments.
- Week 2: short public status update + any blockers.
- Week 4: initial metric snapshot + quick wins.

——
Scratch comments / random prompts (delete or keep for context):
- Should we invite Product Marketing for the Private pilot slide? yes probably.
- Consider a short customer quote about reliability to open (real or anonymized) — ask CS.
- Check with Legal on wording around "no layoffs" claim.

End of scratch.

(If this turns into a polished doc, move action items into a checklist and create a slide template.)
